title: Meridian instance-data migration register
description: Container for migration plans (record_type: instance-migration-plan) — the product-neutral, storage-neutral contract that describes, verifies and reproducibly applies the migration of a transitional Instance's records into Meridian's logical scope areas (workspace-scope-model.md) without choosing a persistent store. Each entry is a scoped record: its envelope (identity, scope, origin, authority) is validated separately against scoped-record.schema.json, and this schema is not a second envelope schema. payload.source pins an explicit revision, a SHA-256 digest and a repository_ref and declares whether the source qualifies as a reproducible base (working_tree_clean required true for 'reproducible'); a 'reproducible' claim is additionally checked at the library level against a snapshot resolved through an EXTERNAL boundary (resolveSourceSnapshot) keyed by (repository_ref, revision) — a claimed value with no resolved, matching snapshot never confirms reproducibility, and a dirty, incomplete, ambiguous or changed source is never accepted as reproducible. payload.record_units and payload.mappings each require at least one entry — an empty migration plan is never valid, though an empty registry container still is. payload.mappings gives each declared unit exactly one correspondence decision — migrated, retained-transitional, or merged (many-to-one, with an explicit shared merge_rule_ref, checked as a GROUP so an undeclared implicit multi-unit 'migrated' is rejected too) — never derived from a file path alone. A migrated or merged target carries an explicit field_basis (preserved vs assigned) for id/record_type/scope/origin/authority, a mandatory origin (kind pinned 'migrated', source_ref checked at the library level to trace to the group's ACTUAL contributing record_unit id(s) — never freely asserted, and field_basis.origin checked to always be 'assigned') and an owner decision; every mapping sharing one target must describe a structurally identical target record; the target's scope carries the SAME structural constraints as workspace-scope-model.md's own scope envelope (built-in-methodology fixes id, repository-scope/run-state require workspace_id); its permanent authority is checked against the closed owner-authority table for its own scope, and the delegated-run authority that carries out the migration itself can never mint a target's permanent authority. payload.rollback is mandatory on every plan and is closed to two MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE variants (deterministic-reconstruction requires deterministic_plan_ref and FORBIDS restoration_evidence_ref; verified-restoration requires restoration_evidence_ref and FORBIDS deterministic_plan_ref — an inactive ref for the other variant is a schema violation, never silently ignored); it is checked at the library level, not merely schema-shaped: source_snapshot_ref is resolved through an EXTERNAL boundary (resolveRollbackSnapshot) and checked to name THIS plan's own source repository_ref/revision/digest; the concrete plan (deterministic-reconstruction's deterministic_plan_ref via resolveDeterministicPlan, or verified-restoration's restoration_evidence_ref via resolveRestorationEvidence) is resolved and checked to name THIS plan's own id AND its own RECOMPUTED plan_fingerprint, plus rollback.source_snapshot_ref — a bare non-empty ref string, invented, cross-plan, cross-snapshot or pinned to a STALE version of this plan's own content, never backs a rollback claim; rewrites_published_history is pinned to the literal false. payload.verification distinguishes a claimed overall_status from actual coverage and applicability-preservation SUB-VERDICTS, each independently checked at the library level: a 'verified' sub-verdict's evidence_ref is resolved through an EXTERNAL boundary (resolveEvidence) and the resolved record must actually confirm THIS plan's id AND its own RECOMPUTED plan_fingerprint (not merely its id) AND THIS kind of result — a non-empty evidence_ref string alone, or one pinned to a stale fingerprint of a plan whose mapping/target/owner_decision has since changed, never backs a verified claim; a not-reproducible source always forces BLOCKED. payload.plan_fingerprint is a documented canonical projection of source/record_units/mappings/rollback, recomputed and checked at the library level — this SAME recomputed fingerprint is what every evidence/rollback proof above is pinned to; payload.idempotency_key is DERIVED from the plan's own scope and the canonical identity of its pinned source — repository_ref, revision AND the full digest, not revision alone, so two different source repositories sharing a revision TEXT never collide (never an arbitrary free-form string) — and unique across the container, so two independently authored plans over one pinned input collide rather than passing as unrelated records; a superseding plan is checked to share its predecessor's FULL scope and SAME source repository_ref and pin a changed source revision — in-document directly, or, when the predecessor is not present in this document, through an EXTERNAL boundary (resolveSupersededPlan) that NEVER accepts an unknown or unresolved predecessor id automatically. The contract is a mandatory part of the Kernel: an absent schema or absent fixtures is a validator FAIL, not an informational skip. The rules JSON Schema cannot state live in scripts/lib/instance-data-migration.mjs. The normative document is standards/workspace/instance-data-migration.md.

source_state.description: The exact, pinned source revision this plan reads from. repository_ref is an opaque identifier of the source Instance, never a filesystem path — property 1 (storage neutrality) and property 2 (precise source): the physical path is never the identity. A 'reproducible' qualification is checked at the library level against a snapshot resolved through an external boundary keyed by (repository_ref, revision); the resolved repository_ref must match (a snapshot resolved for a different repository never confirms this one's reproducibility) and the resolved digest is checked in its full closed form (an extra or missing field inside digest is rejected); a claimed value with no resolved, matching snapshot never confirms reproducibility.

record_unit.description: One declared source unit this plan accounts for. classification_basis is an explicit, human-authored justification of the chosen correspondence — checked at the library level to differ from unit_ref itself, so classification is never claimed to be derived from the path or reference alone.

field_basis.description: Explicit, per-field basis for every field semantics preservation requires (workspace-scope-model.md §2): 'preserved' when the old record already carried it, 'assigned' when the migration itself supplies it. A field the old format never carried can never be silently claimed 'preserved'. origin is checked at the library level to always be 'assigned': a pre-Meridian record never carried this canonical origin shape.

target_scope.description: The SAME structural constraints as workspace-scope-model.md's own scope envelope (scoped-record.schema.json definitions.scope_ref) — not a diverging simplified copy: built-in-methodology fixes id; repository-scope and run-state require workspace_id; only project-workspace may carry organization_profile_id.

target_authority.description: A migrated or merged target's own authority. decision_ref is always required — semantics preservation carries an explicit owner decision, never an implied one (property 4).

target_origin.description: A migrated or merged target's own origin, in the SAME canonical shape as the record envelope's own origin (scoped-record.schema.json definitions.origin). kind is pinned to 'migrated' — a target minted by this contract is always data migrated from a source, never built-in, declared, imported or derived. source_ref is checked at the library level to trace to the canonical reference of the ACTUAL record_unit id(s) contributing to this target — never a freely asserted string (property 4).

mapping.description: One record unit's correspondence decision. 'migrated' and 'merged' mint a target and require an owner_decision; 'merged' additionally requires an explicit merge_rule_ref shared by every mapping merging into the same target (checked at the library level to actually be many-to-one); 'retained-transitional' keeps the unit as a transitional source and requires an explicit retained_reason instead of a target.

rollback.description: Mandatory on every plan (property 5: reversibility by default). plan is closed to exactly two mutually EXCLUSIVE variants: deterministic-reconstruction requires deterministic_plan_ref and forbids restoration_evidence_ref; verified-restoration requires restoration_evidence_ref and forbids deterministic_plan_ref — an inactive ref for the other variant is never silently tolerated, it is a schema violation. The library level (scripts/lib/instance-data-migration.mjs) additionally resolves source_snapshot_ref, deterministic_plan_ref and restoration_evidence_ref through their own EXTERNAL boundaries and checks each against THIS plan's own source, id and exact content (plan_fingerprint) — a bare non-empty ref string is never itself accepted as proof of reversibility. rewrites_published_history is pinned to the literal false — a rollback plan is never a rewrite of published history.

verification.description: Distinguishes a claimed result from actual evidence (property 6): overall_status VERIFIED is checked at the library level against BOTH sub-verdicts and against source.qualification — never merely asserted.
